definition: Relational data mining is the data mining technique for relational databases.
details: Unlike traditional data mining algorithms, which look for patterns in a single table (propositional patterns), relational data mining algorithms look for patterns among multiple tables (relational patterns). For most types of propositional patterns, there are corresponding relational patterns. For example, there are relational classification rules (relational classification), relational regression tree, and relational association rules. There are several approaches to relational data mining: Inductive Logic Programming (ILP) Statistical Relational Learning (SRL) Graph Mining Propositionalization Multi-view learning
story: Think of a historian sorting through boxes of letters, building a picture of an era one sentence at a time. In plain words: Relational data mining is the data mining technique for relational databases. Here is how it actually plays out: Unlike traditional data mining algorithms, which look for patterns in a single table (propositional patterns), relational data mining algorithms look for patterns among multiple tables (relational patterns). The words a model reads become the world it believes in. That care with the raw material is Relational data mining.
